html:
SMTO-AUT-0009 — Sign in to the service so the Task can continue

GUID: 8f4fc110-daba-5ce9-9e21-b85e8d587493
Slug: auth-authorization-required
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: auth-broker

What happened

  • This step uses a connected service that needs you to sign in and approve access first. Until you do, the step waits here and doesn't continue.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Task, find Complete OAuth authorization to continue and select Open authorization page. If a Device code is shown, enter that code on the page. Signing in on the service's own page gives this connection the access the step is waiting for.
  2. Sign in with the account SMTO should use, approve the access, then go back to the SMTO tab. When the service confirms, the page says Authorization complete and the waiting step carries on by itself.
  3. If no sign-in prompt appears, or the page says the authorization expired, ask SMTO in the conversation to try the step again so it shows a new prompt. Each sign-in link works once and only for a short time, so a fresh request creates a new one.

What success looks like

  • The sign-in page says Authorization complete, and the Task continues past the waiting step.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this connection. Don't paste the sign-in link, the device code, or any password into the conversation or the error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The OAuth broker needs user consent (browser or device authorization) for this connection, or could not open that interaction because the request has no owning run or too many authorizations are already pending.

What this means

  • The broker needs a supported user-consent interaction or the saved launch descriptor can no longer be resolved. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • The broker needs a supported user-consent interaction or the saved launch descriptor can no longer be resolved.

How to diagnose it

  • Use the current task's authorization prompt; if its launch link expired, request a fresh interaction for that same connection.

How to fix it

  • Complete the pending authorization from the Task's OAuth prompt (the /api/agent/auth/oauth/start/ ticket link) or with the device code. AuthBroker._interact needs a run context and allows at most 128 pending transactions; if the launch link has expired, restart authorization from the waiting operation rather than reusing the old link.
  • Complete the current browser or device authorization prompt. If its link expired, restart authorization from the waiting operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended connection reaches authorized state and the waiting operation passes its current authority check.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
